newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Kunene Bros eyes merged PQ unit.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Kunene Bros eyes merged PQ unit.

text.p: South Africa's black investment group Kunene Brothers said on Monday it was planning to buy a stake in newly merged information technology group PQ Holdings Ltd in a further step towards black empowerment.

PQ Holdings is to be formed through the merger of Q-Data Holdings Ltd and Persetel Holdings Ltd in a move that will create a group with a market capitalisation of about 12 billion rand ($2.6 billion).
The merged company will have two unlisted divisions PQ Africa and PQ International. Kunene is interested in buying a 51 percent stake in PQ Africa being offered to black-owned companies.
Kunene had previously agreed to buy 28 percent of Grinaker Holdings, of which Q-Data forms a part.

"We have an agreement that we are buying because we had a tentative agreement to buy the AVI (Anglovaal Industries Ltd) stake in Grinaker Holdings which is part of the assets of PQ (Africa)," Kunene Brothers chairman Keith Kunene told Reuters.
He said they would also seek out other black empowerment groups to participate in the deal: "It is people who can add value in this whole thing and see it grow. We can't see it grow alone."

He said the plan would not derail an agreement to buy a 28 percent stake in Grinaker Holdings. "That still goes. It is almost concluded. We had an agreement already, now when this PQ thing came up it meant changing the agreement. So (there are) one or two complications that will be sorted out hopefully before the end of the week," he said.
He would not say what the complications were save that they were technical.

Kunene Brothers already has a 30 percent stake in Grinaker Electronics, a unit of Grinaker Holdings, and would increase this to 35 percent. It also owns Kunene Electronics which is also involved in telecommunications.

Persetel said it was in negotiations with a black empowerment group to take a stake in the group. "We are committed to black empowerment both at the operating and shareholder level," said Rian du Plessis, Persetel director of international finance.

"We were far down the road in our black empowerment initiative at the shareholding level, when the opportunity to talk to Q-Data came along. We then had to interrupt our discussion and we will be taking them up again as soon as the dust settles," he added.
He said it was premature to give any further details and would not comment if the other empowerment group was Consolidated Empowerment Initiative (CEIN).
Persetel in July said it had formed a partnership with CEIN in a bid to reposition itself as a full network systems integrator.
